stem: A client has symmetric pain and swelling in both hands with prolonged morning stiffness. Which finding is more characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis than osteoarthritis?

options.A: Pain mainly with joint use and brief stiffness after rest without persistent inflammatory swelling.
options.B: Symmetric inflammatory involvement of the hands or other small joints with morning stiffness lasting longer than 30 minutes and possible fatigue or low-grade fever.
options.C: Symptoms confined to weight-bearing joints with short morning stiffness and mechanical pain as the dominant pattern.
options.D: Arthritis limited to older adults with no autoimmune inflammation or extra-articular features.

rationale: NIAMS describes rheumatoid arthritis as a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease that often affects joints symmetrically, commonly involving the wrists, hands, and feet. Typical findings include swelling and warmth, morning or post-rest stiffness lasting longer than 30 minutes, fatigue, and occasional low-grade fever. B is the finding more characteristic of RA than a degenerative osteoarthritis pattern.
educational_objective: Differentiate rheumatoid arthritis from a mechanical osteoarthritis pattern by recognizing symmetric inflammatory small-joint disease with prolonged morning stiffness and possible systemic symptoms.
source_organization: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS), NIH
source_locator: Overview and Symptoms of Rheumatoid Arthritis: autoimmune inflammatory disease; often symmetrical; wrists/hands/feet commonly affected; stiffness longer than 30 minutes; fatigue and occasional low-grade fever.
source_claim_supported: RA commonly presents with symmetric inflammatory joint involvement, prolonged morning stiffness over 30 minutes, hand/wrist/foot involvement, and possible fatigue or low-grade fever.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation, printed p.14: recognize pathophysiology and clinical manifestations of chronic physical-health conditions.

source_original.stem: A client has symmetric pain and swelling in both hands with prolonged morning stiffness. Which finding is more characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis than osteoarthritis?

options.A: Look for pain mainly with joint use, brief stiffness after rest, and a predominantly degenerative pattern without persistent synovitis.
options.B: Look for symmetric inflammatory small-joint involvement with morning stiffness longer than 30 minutes and possible fatigue or low-grade fever.
options.C: Look for symptoms confined to weight-bearing joints with short morning stiffness and mechanical pain as the dominant pattern.
options.D: Look for arthritis limited to older adults with no autoimmune inflammation or extra-articular features as the defining pattern.

source_original.rationale: NIAMS describes RA as a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease that often affects joints symmetrically, especially wrists/hands/feet, with morning stiffness longer than 30 minutes and possible fatigue or fever.
source_original.source_detail: Symptoms of Rheumatoid Arthritis. NIAMS page last reviewed 2022-11; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Physiological Adaptation, printed p.14: acute/chronic alterations, emergency response and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained key B and the RA-versus-mechanical-arthritis distinction, tightened the keyed option to NIAMS-supported features, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.exact_locator: NIAMS RA Overview and Symptoms sections
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses symmetric inflammatory involvement, >30-minute stiffness and systemic features directly supported by NIAMS.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect for the described RA pattern; emphasizes mechanical/degenerative features.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; confined weight-bearing mechanical pattern is not characteristic of RA.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; RA is autoimmune, may occur beyond older age, and can have extra-articular features.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B matches the full inflammatory symmetric pattern.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe arthritis patterns and require clinical discrimination.
audit_findings.blueprint: Physiological Adaptation — chronic autoimmune musculoskeletal disease.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read current NIAMS RA page, all options, rationale and NCSBN mapping. B remained uniquely correct.
